title: Spell a name
goal: Recognise, name and write M, A, Y.
cue: Names use capital and lowercase letters. Letter names help us spell; word sounds help us read words.
spelling: Names use capital and lowercase letters. Letter names help us spell; word sounds help us read words.
rhythm: M   A   Y   B   E   N
task: Say your name. Spell it one letter at a time. Ask someone to repeat the letters back.
story: May is a name. It has three letters: M, A, Y. A name starts with a capital letter.
reviewPrompt: Recall two letters from day 10 before looking back.

cards.title: Letter M
sections: In map, m represents /m/. This is a word sound, not the letter name.
Write M and m three times. Cover the model and write the pair again.

articulation.label: Letter M
articulation.alt: Letter M: /ɛ/ → /m/. Tongue, lips, contact and airflow positions.
notes: /ɛ/: Front tongue; open the jaw a little more.
/m/: Close both lips; air goes through the nose.
articulation.note: Join the sounds smoothly after practising each position.

cards.title: Letter A
sections: In apple, a represents /æ/. This is a word sound, not the letter name.
Write A and a three times. Cover the model and write the pair again.

articulation.label: Letter A
articulation.alt: Letter A: /eɪ/. Tongue, lips, contact and airflow positions.
notes: /ɪ/: Raise the front tongue; narrow the jaw gap.
articulation.note: Keep each vowel glide inside one syllable.

cards.title: Letter Y
sections: yogurt /ˈjoʊɡɚt/ · a food made from milk
In yogurt, y represents /j/. This is a word sound, not the letter name.
Write Y and y three times. Cover the model and write the pair again.

articulation.label: Letter Y
articulation.alt: Letter Y: /w/ → /aɪ/. Tongue, lips, contact and airflow positions.
notes: /w/: Round the lips; raise the back of the tongue.
/a/: Start with the tongue low and jaw open.
/ɪ/: Glide up and forward; narrow the jaw gap.
articulation.note: Keep each vowel glide inside one syllable.

cards.title: Five words to hear and use
sections: the word people call you. My name is Heart.
a greeting when you meet someone. Hello, Puck!
a person you know and like. This is my friend.
a person who helps others learn. Heart is a teacher.
a person who is learning at a school or on a course. I’m a student.
Listen to each word. Point or act to show its meaning. Say one word, then one short sentence. Ask for help with spelling patterns you have not learned yet.
